# Triss Coworker

> Managed delegation for AI development: an open-source CLI and MCP server (npm package `triss-coworker`, binary `triss`) that delegates codebase research, code review, and implementation tasks from coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) to the model providers and coding engines the user configures. Local-first, no telemetry, MIT-licensed. Canonical site: https://triss.work. The short name for "Triss Coworker" is "Triss".

Install: `npm install -g triss-coworker` (requires Node.js >= 22.12). MCP tools are named `triss_ask`, `triss_review`, `triss_fetch`, `triss_chat`, `triss_write`, `triss_commit_msg`, `triss_status`. Call `triss agent-help` locally for the full delegation cookbook.

## When to use this

- Delegate codebase research from a coding agent: ask questions over selected paths or URLs and get evidence-backed answers (`triss ask`, MCP `triss_ask`).
- Get a code review of a branch, pull request, selected files, or a piped diff (`triss review`, MCP `triss_review`).
- Hand a bounded implementation task to a separate coding agent through a configurable engine (OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Crush, OMP) with Git worktree separation (`triss coder run`).
- Fetch a web page as readable Markdown with bounded redirects (`triss fetch`, MCP `triss_fetch`), or run a one-shot prompt (`triss chat`).
- Generate a Conventional Commits message from staged changes (`triss commit-msg`).

## When not to use this

- You need a hosted service, dashboard, or cloud API — Triss is a local CLI + MCP server with no control plane.
- You want unattended, no-review automation — completed runs are results to inspect, not accepted work; a human decides what ships.
- The task is unrelated to software development workflows (research delegation, review, implementation, trackers).

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://triss.work/docs/getting-started/): install, wizard, first delegation.
- [Documentation](https://triss.work/docs/): provider and model configuration, engines, integration setup.
- [Command reference](https://triss.work/commands/): every CLI command and MCP tool with flags and examples.
- [Workflows](https://triss.work/workflows/): research, review, and implementation recipes for host agents.
- [Coding engines](https://triss.work/coder/): engine selection, isolation model, credential proxy.
- [Costs](https://triss.work/cost/): delegation pricing methodology and calculator.

## Machine-readable resources

- [llms-full.txt](https://triss.work/llms-full.txt): the usage-critical docs as one Markdown file.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://triss.work/openapi.json): the public read-only JSON API surface (OpenAPI 3.1).
- [API: meta](https://triss.work/api/v1/meta): package identity, version, install command.
- [API: commands](https://triss.work/api/v1/commands): the command catalogue as JSON.
- [API: docs](https://triss.work/api/v1/docs): index of pages with their Markdown mirrors.
- [Sitemap](https://triss.work/sitemap-index.xml): all public pages.

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ayleen/triss-coworker): source, issues, releases.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/triss-coworker): published CLI package (note: the bare `triss` name on npm is an unrelated package).
- [Security](https://triss.work/security/): trust boundary and data flows in plain language.
- [Privacy](https://triss.work/privacy/): what is stored locally and what may leave the machine.
- [About](https://triss.work/about/): what the project is and how it is maintained.
- [Contact](https://triss.work/contact/): where to report bugs, vulnerabilities, and send patches.
